## Catalog Description

Survey of Optimization. (3-0). Credit 3. Theory and numerical methods for deterministic linear and nonlinear optimization; topics include linear programming, unconstrained-nonlinear optimization, constrained-nonlinear optimization, Lagrange and K-K-T conditions, and numerical algorithms. Prerequisite: MATH 304 or MATH 311.

## Course Learning Outcomes

Upon completion of this course, the learner will be able to:

- Analyze and apply linear and nonlinear programming theory and algorithms.

- Formulate linear and nonlinear optimization models from real-world problems.

- Solve small-scale optimization problems by hand and utilize optimization software to solve large-scale problems.

## Special Course Designation

None

## Grading Policy

### Assessments

Your grade will be based upon:

1. Midterm I (25% of total grade subject to replacement) : You will have a midterm that will occur during one of the lectures in roughly late September/early October. See replacement policy under Final Exam, Part I. If you are unable to take this exam for any reason then your Final Exam, Part I grade will replace it.
2. Midterm II (25% of total grade subject to replacement) : You will have a midterm that will occur during one of the recitation periods located roughly in the middle of November. See replacement policy under Final Exam, Part I.
3. Final Exam, Part I (25% of total grade) : The final exam will have two sections that will be graded separately. The first section will cover the same material as midterm I. If your grade on this part exceeds your grade on midterm I, then it will also replace your midterm I grade.
4. Final Exam, Part II (25% of total grade) : The second section will cover the same material as midterm II. If your grade on this part exceeds your grade on midterm II, then it will also replace your midterm II grade.
Attendance is not graded.

#### Additional Course Information

##### Ungraded Homework

Each course topic may be accompanied by an optional, ungraded homework. I will not post solutions to the homework. However, we will offer feedback on your (optionally) submitted solutions. This is you best opportunity to get feedback on your understanding of course material. I must emphasize that turning in or not turning in the optional homework will have NO impact on your grade. Moreover, your performance on the homework will have no impact on your grade.
These homeworks must be turned in by the assigned deadline.

##### Electronic Device Use Policy

The use of any and all electronic devices is explicitly forbidden with a single exception. You may use an tablet or laptop computer to take notes but only if you sit in one of the front X rows, where the number X will be determined by the conclusion of the second class session. If you are sitting in one of these rows and using one of your devices for tasks other than note taking then this will be considered an electronic device use policy violation.
The first electronic device use policy violation will result in a warning. Each subsequent violation will result in a one letter course grade deduction.

##### Academic Integrity

Any instance of cheating or plagiarism will be referred to the Aggie Honor Council. The recommended penalty will be failure of the course.
